title: PBMCs from CTEPH patient, replicate 1, scRNAseq
characteristics_ch1: cell type: PBMCs, including T cells, B cells, NK cells, and monocytes
extract_protocol_ch1: Venous blood (2 mL) was collected into an EDTA anticoagulant tube and immediately transported to the laboratory on ice for subsequent scRNA-seq analysis. To ensure viability and integrity of the cells, the blood was processed within two hours of collection. Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells (PBMCs) were isolated using density gradient centrifugation with Ficoll-Paque Plus medium (GE Healthcare). Following this, red blood cells were lysed using 2 mL of GEXSCOPE® Red Blood Cell Lysis Buffer (RCLB, Singleron) at 25°C for 10 minutes. The lysed sample was then centrifuged at 500 × g for 5 minutes, and the supernatant was discarded. The remaining cells were washed and centrifuged twice at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove any residual lysis buffer. Finally, the PBMCs were resuspended in phosphate-buffered saline to create a single-cell suspension, ready for downstream scRNA-seq library preparation.

Single-cell suspensions (2×105 cells/mL) were prepared using PBS (HyClone), and then the single-cell suspension was loaded onto a microwell chip using the Singleron Matrix® Single Cell Processing System. GEXSCOPE® Single Cell RNA Library Kits (Singleron) were used for single-cell capture and library construction according to the manufacturer's specifications. Sequencing was performed on the Illumina HiSeq X and Illumina Novaseq 6000 platforms.
